I’d like to make a change to the onboarding flow so new users can experience the app before the paywall appears.

Before implementing anything, I want to clearly document the current flow and the desired change so this is implemented safely.

Current Flow

User downloads the app

Welcome screen appears with the “Start Free Trial” button

Apple subscription/paywall appears

User completes profile setup

User enters the tracking screen

Desired New Flow

I want new users to be able to experience the app for their first 24 hours before seeing the paywall.

The flow should be:

User downloads the app

Welcome screen appears

The “Start Free Trial” button should be changed to “Get Started” so the user can enter the app without triggering the subscription yet

User completes profile setup

User enters the tracking screen and can use the app normally (including the plate visualization and portion tracking)

The user should have full access during their first 24 hours after first launch.

Paywall Trigger

After the first 24 hours:

The next time the user opens the app (or attempts to continue using it), the existing paywall should appear.

Once the paywall appears:

The 7-day free trial

The monthly and annual subscription options

Restore purchases

should all work exactly the same as they do today.

I do not want to change the subscription setup itself, only the timing of when the paywall appears.

Important

Please implement this in the simplest and safest way possible without changing the existing Apple subscription configuration.

Let me know if this approach fits the current architecture or if you recommend a safer way to implement the 24-hour delayed paywall.

attributes.gen_ai.skill.content:
# RevenueCat Skill

## Setup

When the user wants subscriptions, paywalls, in-app purchases, premium features, pro versions, or monetization: ALWAYS use the `setup_revenuecat` tool. NEVER write subscription code manually.

The tool generates all required files:
- `contexts/SubscriptionContext.tsx` — Subscription provider with RevenueCat SDK
- `app/paywall.tsx` — Paywall screen with purchase UI and pricing

It also auto-integrates `SubscriptionProvider` into `app/_layout.tsx` and wires the paywall into the onboarding flow.

### Arguments

- `entitlement_id`: The RevenueCat entitlement identifier (default: `"pro"`).
- `premium_features`: List of 3–4 features for the paywall. Each item needs `icon` (lucide icon name), `title`, and `description`. Always tailor these to the app:
  - Fitness app: `{icon: "Dumbbell", title: "Unlimited Workouts", description: "Access all workout programs"}`
  - Notes app: `{icon: "Cloud", title: "Cloud Sync", description: "Sync across all devices"}`
  - Recipe app: `{icon: "BookOpen", title: "Unlimited Recipes", description: "Save unlimited recipes"}`

### After calling setup_revenuecat

Verify in the tool output:
1. `SubscriptionProvider` was added to `_layout.tsx` (add manually if it failed)
2. Paywall is integrated into the onboarding flow

## Troubleshooting

If the user reports subscription issues (no products showing, purchases failing):
1. Call `diagnose_revenuecat` first — it runs a full diagnostic and returns actionable findings.
2. Call `get_revenuecat_status` if you need additional context about the current connection state.

Do NOT attempt to fix subscription issues by editing subscription code manually before running the diagnostic tools.
